Minimizer Quick Guide

This page introduces Minimizer module, which provides the global-fit cost function and iMinuit-based minimization driver used in GUMP.

The module is analysis-specific (data selection, cuts, and fit strategy are hard-wired), but it is the central entry point for reproducing the published fit workflow.

What this module does

At a high level, Minimizer:

  • loads and preprocesses all fit datasets (PDF/tPDF, GFF, GPD, DVCS, DVMP),

  • computes theory predictions from parameter vectors,

  • builds per-point residual costs,

  • adds sum-rule penalty terms,

  • minimizes the total \(\chi^2\) with iMinuit.

Core APIs

Primary fit interfaces:

  • Minimizer.cost_off_forward_withH_withHt(): full global cost function.

  • Minimizer.off_forward_fit_withH_withHt(): iMinuit setup + MIGRAD + HESSE driver.

Important theory wrappers used inside the cost function:

  • PDF/GFF/GPD sector: Minimizer.PDF_theo(), Minimizer.GFF_theo(), Minimizer.GPD_theo()

  • DVCS/DVMP sector: Minimizer.DVCSxsec_theo(), Minimizer.DVCSAsym_theo(), Minimizer.DVCSxsecHERA_theo(), Minimizer.DVMPxsec_theo()

  • Amplitude-level helpers: Minimizer.CFF_theo(), Minimizer.TFF_theo()

Parallel execution is handled through a shared process pool:

  • Minimizer.get_pool()

  • Minimizer.close_pool()

  • Minimizer.group_by_unique()

Fit parameters

The iMinuit cost signature is flat (one argument per parameter), while the implementation groups parameters into three blocks:

  • Paralst_Unp_Names: unpolarized parameters,

  • Paralst_Pol_Names: polarized parameters,

  • Paralst_Aux_Names: auxiliary parameters (currently jpsinorm).

Internally these are validated by Minimizer.validate_params() and then converted with gumpgpd.Parameters.ParaManager_Unp() and gumpgpd.Parameters.ParaManager_Pol().

Cost-function structure

The total objective is:

\[\chi^2_{\mathrm{total}} = \chi^2_{\mathrm{exp}} + \chi^2_{\mathrm{PDF/GFF/GPD}} + \chi^2_{\mathrm{penalty}}.\]

where:

  • \(\chi^2_{\mathrm{exp}}\) comes from DVCS/DVMP observables,

  • \(\chi^2_{\mathrm{PDF/GFF/GPD}}\) comes from PDF-like constraints,

  • \(\chi^2_{\mathrm{penalty}}\) enforces sum-rule constraints with configurable tolerances.

In export mode (config.Export_Mode = True), the cost function can return grouped prediction DataFrames and write CSV outputs via Minimizer.Export_Frame_Append().

Running a fit

Use Minimizer.off_forward_fit_withH_withHt() with initial parameter arrays in the exact order of Paralst_Unp_Names, Paralst_Pol_Names, and Paralst_Aux_Names.

The routine:

  1. builds a iminuit.Minuit object,

  2. applies parameter bounds/fixes,

  3. runs migrad then hesse,

  4. writes a fit summary under GUMP_Output.

Note: keep config.Export_Mode = False during minimization. Use export mode only for post-fit prediction dumping.
